# Merchant Center

*Product* · also written Google Merchant Center · GMC

Google's tool where retailers submit product data (feeds) that Google Shopping, free listings and AI shopping experiences use.

**Glossary** (*Merchant Center*): Google's tool through which merchants send product data feeds for Shopping ads, Search ads and organic results. Products need it to appear in the Shopping tab; product rich results do not.

Narrative: the topic [Shopping data: feeds, markup and Storebot](../topics/shopping-data.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

31 claims mention it: 14 from Google's documentation, 11 shown or said at the event (2 not in Google docs, 5 confirmed by Google docs, 4 consistent with Google docs), 6 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Product data specification](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7052112?hl=en), [Free listings for products](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en), [Allow Merchant Center to update product information automatically](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284?hl=en).

- [`D2-C005`](../sessions/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) Docs: Google's ecommerce documentation recommends linking from menus to category pages, from category pages to sub-category pages and from sub-category pages to all product pages; where not every product can be linked, it recommends a sitemap or a Merchant Center feed. `[D2-C005, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/help-google-understand-your-ecommerce-site-structure]`
- [`D2-C507`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Docs: Google's documentation updates log calls the July 2026 sale price change a clarification: a new Sale duration section of the merchant listing guide explains validFrom with validThrough or priceValidUntil, aligned with Merchant Center's sale_price_effective_date attribute. `[D2-C507, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/updates]`
- [`D3-C344`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Docs: Google's Product structured data introduction says that providing both on-page structured data and a Merchant Center feed maximizes eligibility for shopping experiences and helps Google understand and verify the data; product snippets may take pricing from the feed when the markup lacks it. `[D3-C344, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product]`
- [`D3-C347`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Docs: Google's Merchant Center help says products and details crawled from an online store can show up on Google even when they are not marked up with schema.org or added in Merchant Center, and lists the Shopping tab among the places Merchant Center free listings appear. `[D3-C347, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C350`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Docs: Merchant Center's automatic item updates use structured data and other product data found on landing pages to fix price, sale price, availability and condition mismatches in a merchant's product data; Google says they do not replace regular feed updates. `[D3-C350, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C361`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: On 11 January 2026 Google announced 'dozens of new data attributes' in Merchant Center for conversational commerce on AI Mode, Gemini and Business Agent, to roll out first with a small group of retailers. `[D3-C361, docs, Google blog (11 January 2026), https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/agentic-commerce-ai-tools-protocol-retailers-platforms/]`
- [`D3-C362`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: At Google Marketing Live on 20 May 2026 Google said retailers globally can now use conversational attributes in Merchant Center to reflect the more conversational way people search. `[D3-C362, docs, Google blog (20 May 2026), https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/shopping/shopping-updates-google-marketing-live/]`
- [`D3-C367`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Google's Merchant Center help marks the question_and_answer, document_link, related_product and popularity_rank attributes as primarily intended for conversational experiences such as AI Mode in Google Search. `[D3-C367, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085211?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C369`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Merchant Center's question_and_answer attribute takes up to 30 question-and-answer pairs per product, each question and answer up to 1,000 characters and 10,000 characters in total, and must not contain prices, shipping, dates or the company name. `[D3-C369, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7052112?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C371`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Merchant Center's document_link attribute takes up to five URLs of PDF documents about a product, such as manuals, user guides or assembly instructions, and the merchant must own the content licensing rights. `[D3-C371, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17084656?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C375`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Merchant Center's popularity_rank is a 0-100 value the merchant assigns to rank a product's popularity, based on its recent sales, against the rest of its own inventory; it does not reflect user ratings. `[D3-C375, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085297?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C388`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Google's Merchant Center help says the StoreBot crawler goes through product detail, cart and checkout pages, can fill in checkout forms, and records price, shipping, availability, coupons and payment methods to verify the data merchants share in Merchant Center. `[D3-C388, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/13294660?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C393`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Merchant Center's product_highlight attribute takes 2 to 100 highlights of up to 150 characters each that describe only the product itself, without promotional text, keywords or search terms. `[D3-C393, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12471629?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C395`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Merchant Center's product_detail attribute takes up to 100 specifications, each a section name, attribute name and attribute value, and Google's help says clean key-value specifications improve product details on Google Shopping and AI-driven surfaces. `[D3-C395, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9218260?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C352`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google's Merchant Center feed specification is how millions of merchants send Google billions of product offers, which are used in Shopping ads, Search ads and organic search results. `[D3-C352, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C399`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: A recent schema.org release added two properties, specification and valueGroup, so that the Merchant Center product detail attribute can be expressed in schema.org, with product specs nested under specification. `[D3-C399, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C343`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google Search displays product rich results from product structured data; it may also use the product data a merchant provides in Google Merchant Center, but Merchant Center is not required for them. `[D3-C343, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C349`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Product structured data can help Merchant Center in some cases, for example during data validation, but Merchant Center does not require it. `[D3-C349, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C365`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google added six Merchant Center feed attributes for AI shopping experiences: question and answer, documents, related products, item group title and variant option for variants, and popularity rank. `[D3-C365, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C392`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google now emphasises two existing Merchant Center attributes for AI, product highlights (a short bulleted list) and product detail (detailed specifications), and updated its Help Center guidance to say they help AI systems. `[D3-C392, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C407`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google Shopping pointed to a Google holiday shopping blog post with early results from real merchants using the conversational attributes, and to the Merchant Center Help Center and schema.org for the attributes and properties. `[D3-C407, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C345`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Product annotations on Google Images results also come from product structured data and do not need Google Merchant Center. `[D3-C345, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C346`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: To appear in the Shopping tab of Google Search, a product must be submitted in Google Merchant Center; product structured data alone is not enough. `[D3-C346, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C359`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: In 2026, a few months before the October event, Google added new Merchant Center feed attributes to help AI systems understand product nuances, prompted by feedback since 2025 from merchants worried whether AI experiences represented them correctly. `[D3-C359, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C397`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google named the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), next to the Merchant Center feed, as an industry standard whose capabilities it also wants schema.org to cover. `[D3-C397, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C508`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Analysis: For time-limited sales, give the sale price its validity dates in the product markup (Google's merchant listing documentation describes validFrom, validThrough and priceValidUntil) instead of editing markup by hand when the sale ends, and keep the dates aligned with the Merchant Center feed. `[D2-C508, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C348`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Analysis: Google's free listings help says crawled store products can appear on Google without markup or Merchant Center but does not say whether that includes the Shopping tab; for a shop that wants Shopping tab visibility, the stage rule that Merchant Center is required is the safe working assumption. `[D3-C348, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C351`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Analysis: For an online shop, Product structured data is enough for product rich results and Google Images product annotations, but the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed too; keep feed and markup values identical, since Google can use the markup to validate the feed. `[D3-C351, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C366`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Analysis: Google's January 2026 announcement spoke of 'dozens' of new Merchant Center attributes, while the Day 3 talk counted six; all six named on stage (question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, item_group_title, variant_option, popularity_rank) are in the Merchant Center product data specification as of 3 October 2026. `[D3-C366, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C381`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Analysis: As of 3 October 2026 Google's Merchant Center help lists no schema.org property for question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, popularity_rank, variant_option or product_detail (only item_group_title maps, to ProductGroup.name), and Search Central does not document such markup: reading these attributes from schema.org is a stage statement, the feed is the documented route. `[D3-C381, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C410`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Analysis: Shop developers should first keep core feed and markup values (price, availability, brand, GTIN) accurate, then add Q&As, product highlights, specs as key-value product details and related products in the Merchant Center feed, and mirror them in schema.org Product markup only as Google documents support for it. `[D3-C410, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-SDA-08` **SHOULD** · Documented: Mark up merchant listings completely, with validity dates for sale prices (2 of its claims mention it)
- `DEV-SHP-01` **SHOULD** · Documented: Use Product markup for rich results and a Merchant Center feed for the Shopping tab, with identical values (7 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SHP-03` **SHOULD** · Documented: Send conversational product data in the Merchant Center feed: Q&A, product details, highlights and related products (8 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SHP-04` **MAY** · Said at Search Central Live: Treat product Q&A and specification markup in schema.org as an extra on top of the feed (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
